britannica-1911-kyshtym: Kyshtym is a town of Russia, in the government of Perm, 56 miles by rail N.N.W. of Chelyabinsk. It stands on a river of the same name, which links two lakes, and in 1897 it held 12,331 people. Its official name is Verkhne-Kyshtymskiy-Zavod, or Upper Kyshtym Works. That name sets it apart from the Lower Kyshtym Works, which lie two miles farther down the same river.
doe-osti-17091588-new-uses-for-known-mol:
James Lewicki of Lawrence Livermore reports in October 2026 on turning known explosive molecules into binder plastics with energy of their own. Current bonded explosives, where crystals are held in a plastic binder, struggle to meet strength targets for next generation uses, and supply is a concern. His approach changes energetics already in use into linked polymers that grip the crystals.

A loop of computer modeling, small scale synthesis, and small scale testing screened options without long bench work. Three chemical systems emerged as strong picks for use in insensitive high explosives. Composites with firm setting binders showed clear gains in strength, and the binder itself added energy to the blast. Advanced simulations suggest strength can approach the limit set by the crystal layers.
